title: Dishman Carbogen Amcis Ltd - 540701 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 19% to INR 851 crore, with EBITDA of INR 163 crore (19.1%) despite INR 30 crore extra onerous-contract provisions.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 851 crore, up about 19% YoY, with CDMO up 21% to INR 690.8 crore and marketable molecules up 9.3% to INR 160.5 crore. EBITDA was about INR 163 crore (19.1% margin), held back by roughly INR 50 crore higher other expenses from onerous-contract provisions and a one-off CHF 2.5 million Swiss pension provision. For FY26, revenue was INR 2,932 crore (up about 8%), EBITDA INR 565 crore (19.3%, up 200 bps) and PAT INR 97.4 crore versus INR 3.2 crore. Management announced a promoter-entity 10-year unsecured external commercial borrowing, subject to shareholder approval, to repay high-cost Indian debt.

financial_highlights.change: up close to 19% YoY from INR 716 crore
up about 21% YoY from INR 569 crore
CDMO up about 6.5%, marketable molecules up about 17%
down about CHF 11 million from CHF 157.6 million

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA margin 18.7% versus 23.9% a year earlier, as Q4 FY25 had high-margin late Phase 3 deliveries; Q4 FY26 carried more commercial supplies and onerous-contract provisions. CDMO was about 81% of Q4 revenue and 83% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Marketable molecules (Vitamin D analogs, cholesterol)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 21.1% in Q4 and 18.8% for FY26, up about 940 bps on the year, helped by higher Vitamin D analog share and supplier diversification (wool grease).

guidance_outlook: Management is cautious on FY27 guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty; an analyst's 22-23% FY27 growth figure was described as the target, with formal guidance to follow after about one quarter.
EBITDA margin target of 25% in FY28 for both segments.
Consolidated revenue CAGR of about 15% over the next three years.

India revenue of about INR 500 crore targeted for FY28; FY27 India revenue expected to rise about 25% from FY26 (about INR 220 crore), with the INR 400 crore FY25 level flagged as possibly difficult in FY27.

Net interest cost of not more than about INR 70 crore for FY27 after refinancing, versus about INR 100 crore consolidated FY26; quarterly interest of INR 30-35 crore seen from Q2 or Q3 FY27 if refinancing goes through.
Group effective tax rate about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years.
Net debt reduction target of at least CHF 10-15 million (about INR 150 crore) every year.
French subsidiary FY27 revenue of EUR 11-12 million and EBITDA loss narrowing to about EUR 6 million; EBITDA breakeven aimed for FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about CHF 22.4 million; no major capex planned beyond the Japanese innovator co-investment, which is 100% partner-funded, plus maintenance and SAP/digital spend.
Engineering for Swiss co-investments is on track; the last manufacturing line in France went live in Q4 FY25.
India capacity is in place and regulatory hurdles are cleared, according to management; India operating margin historically about 35-40%.
Tech transfer of a large Swiss molecule to India has started; it is expected to take several years, with an interim phase-wise move of intermediates.
French site has ANSM approval (about one year before the call) and is bidding for Phase 3 and commercial projects.
demand_pricing: More than 10 late-phase projects in drug substance, including PPQ campaigns; more than 30 commercial products form the revenue base.
ADC and linker-payload demand is strong and high-margin; ADC was about 25% of CDMO revenue in FY26, with purchase orders in hand for the next years.
Management expects ADC linker supply of CHF 30-40 million in FY27 and FY28 per the earlier indicator, and says the margin on this product could be more than double the consolidated margin.

India: a large innovator's tech transfer from Switzerland (CHF 20-25 million annual revenue currently in Switzerland; India could see about CHF 15-20 million after a roughly 30% customer discount) and a second innovator opportunity (at least CHF 20-25 million) are in progress.
Sprint initiative to win early-phase projects is reporting new big pharma and mid/small pharma clients; the sales force was expanded in both Europe and India.
Target CDMO/marketable molecules mix of about 85:15 over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: How should depreciation and tax rate be modelled for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has been broadly flat QoQ in functional currency, with FX translation adding to INR figures. Effective tax rate is seen at about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years as loss-making subsidiaries turn profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Will interest cost fall after refinancing, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly interest could be INR 30-35 crore, conservatively from Q2 or Q3 FY27, after replacing about INR 800 crore of Indian debt costing about 10.5-11% with cheaper promoter-entity borrowing at about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FX risk from the Swiss-franc borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Swiss-franc revenue from India and subsidiaries acts as a natural hedge, so no hedging is planned. It cited India revenue of about INR 5,000 crore in foreign currency over the 10-year tenor against about INR 800 crore of debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 India outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 India revenue and profit are expected to be above FY26, with FY28 target of about INR 500 crore; the FY27 figure may be below the INR 400 crore mentioned. Management said the target holds whether or not the Swiss tech transfer proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill increase from INR 4,054 crore to INR 4,798 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was purely FX restatement at closing rates, with no additions. About INR 550 crore is standalone India goodwill from the 2017 merger and the rest is consolidation goodwill.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise and cash build up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said syndicated facilities were drawn to avoid commitment fees and the USD proceeds are held as deposits earning interest, while Swiss-franc borrowing costs under 4%. Management said net debt is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What is the French subsidiary outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 French revenue was about EUR 8 million with EBITDA loss of about EUR 9 million. FY27 target is EUR 11-12 million revenue and about EUR 6 million loss; breakeven is aimed for FY28, which the analyst noted had slipped.

risks_watch: Onerous-contract provisions (INR 30 crore YoY swing in Q4) and project hour overruns could keep hitting margins.
Shareholder approval and execution timing of the promoter-entity ECB, which is central to the interest-cost savings; the analyst pushed back on the INR 2,500 crore gross debt and leverage level.
India ramp-up depends on tech transfers and innovator orders; visibility on the INR 500 crore FY28 target depends on contracts that are still pending.
Management said molecules can drop out even in late Phase 3, a risk for ADC and CDMO revenue.
FY27 guidance deferred, and the CHF 20-25 million India tech transfer timing is uncertain.
Quarterly phasing of ADC supplies is hard to predict, and management said QoQ comparisons are difficult.
Swiss-franc movements affect INR reported numbers, and the analyst noted a roughly 6-7% CHF depreciation against INR over six months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets such as 25% EBITDA margin in FY28 and the India ramp, but cautious on near-term guidance, which management deferred by about one quarter citing geopolitical uncertainty. Management was defensive when pressed on the rise in debt and the currency-hedge logic, and gave more direct answers on interest cost and cash flow.
key_quotes: We are pretty confident of the growth that we have set out, the path that we have set out in terms of the revenues, the profitability, and the growth plans remain very much intact.
Our target remains the same, which is to get to the 25% mark in the year after next, that is FY28.
So, getting to INR 500 crores is not unrealistic, whether this tech transfer happens or does not happen, because we have multiple projects in the pipeline.
We are not getting more leverage. That is what I would like to correct here.

adds.what: Japanese innovator co-investment (100% partner-funded capex; no company capex)
India tech transfer of a large Swiss molecule (interim phase-wise intermediates move; multi-year)

growth.why: Management guides ~15% revenue CAGR over three years, with FY28 India revenue of INR 500 crore-plus and 25% EBITDA margin by FY28, backed by ADC linker orders (CHF 30-40 million FY27-28), India tech transfers (CHF 15-20 million) and a sprint for early-phase wins, but withholds formal FY27 guidance and has no major capex beyond partner-funded co-investment.
